mainTopic: The ox-goad decree (מרדע) as one of the י״ח דברים, the eighteen decrees. רבי טרפון says the ruling was misunderstood, רבי עקיבא defends it, רבי ינאי explains it, and the גמרא makes sure the count of eighteen still works for רבי טרפון.
overview: This amud continues the list of the eighteen decrees made on one day. רבי טרפון swears that the ox-goad (מרדע) decree is a garbled הלכה. רבי עקיבא defends it by spelling out exactly who becomes טמא and at what size, and רבי ינאי explains that it is a decree on an object whose circumference is a טפח. The גמרא asks how רבי טרפון still reaches eighteen. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that he counts the decree on the daughters of כותים and follows רבי מאיר on drawn water. Next comes the decree on grapes picked for the wine press, which שמאי and הלל argued about. The גמרא tells the story of the sword in the בית המדרש, the day that was as hard as the day of the Golden Calf, and how the decree was accepted only from the students. It then asks for the reason behind the decree: זעירי in the name of רבי חנינא gives impure baskets and then pitched baskets, while רבא points to clusters stuck together. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to name another of the decrees, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי טרפון says the ox-goad ruling was misunderstood
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון swears that the ox-goad decree is a mistake. The original rule only said the ox goad itself becomes טמא when it hangs over a grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: I will bury my sons if this is not a cut-off, garbled הלכה! Someone heard a rule and got it wrong. The real rule was this: a farmer was walking with his ox goad on his shoulder, and one side of it hung over a grave. The חכמים declared the goad itself טמא, because of the rule about vessels that overshadow a dead body.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון rejects the decree that a thick movable object passes טומאה to others. He says the listener confused it with a different, simpler rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the original case, the ox goad is over the grave, so the goad itself becomes טמא. That is a simple law about any vessel overshadowing a מת. רבי טרפון claims someone turned this into a bigger rule: that the goad acts like a tent and passes טומאה onward. He says that bigger rule was never said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I will bury my sons.' This is an oath of strong certainty.
A 'truncated' or garbled ruling, passed down incorrectly.
An ox goad, the long stick a farmer uses to prod cattle.
Overshadowed or covered. This is the root of אוהל (tent) טומאה.
Vessels that overshadow a dead body. They become טמא themselves.

steps.confusionAlert: The oath 'אקפח את בני שזו הלכה מקופחת' literally reads 'that this is a truncated הלכה.' The meaning is 'I swear this IS a garbled ruling.' He is NOT denying that it is garbled.
steps.whyThisMatters: If רבי טרפון is right, this decree drops off the list of eighteen. That sets up the counting question in step 4.

phrases.english: I will bury my sons
phrases.notes: This is a way of swearing an oath.

phrases.english: if this is not a truncated ruling,
that the listener heard and erred:
the farmer was passing with his ox goad on his shoulder
and one side of it overshadowed the grave —
they declared it impure,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the goad itself, not the farmer or other objects.

phrases.english: because of the law of vessels that overshadow a corpse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲקַפֵּחַ אֶת בָּנַי שֶׁזּוֹ הֲלָכָה מְקוּפַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the ox-goad decree listed earlier in the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ox goad over a grave only becomes טמא itself. It does not act as a tent that passes טומאה to others.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא explains the decree so it stands
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא defends the decree by stating exact limits. A thick movable object makes its carrier טמא. It becomes טמא itself at any size. It passes טומאה to other people and vessels only if it is a טפח wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: I will fix the explanation so that the words of the חכמים remain standing. All movable objects bring טומאה onto the person carrying them, if they are as thick as an ox goad. They bring טומאה onto themselves at any size. But onto other people and vessels, they bring טומאה only if they are a טפח wide.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers רבי טרפון. He keeps the decree, but explains exactly who becomes טמא and at what size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא sets up three levels. (1) The person carrying the object becomes טמא if the object is goad-thick. This is the decree. (2) The object itself becomes טמא at any size. (3) Other people and vessels become טמא only through a full טפח opening, which is the Torah's tent measure. This way the decree is real but limited, so the חכמים were not mistaken.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I will correct' or 'I will set it right.' He offers a proper explanation.
Movable objects.
At the thickness of an ox goad.
At any size at all.
An opening (width) of one handbreadth. This is the Torah's minimum for a tent.

steps.whyThisMatters: These three levels are the working rule of the ox-goad decree according to the view that it is one of the eighteen.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said: I will correct it
so that the words of the Sages remain standing:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהוּ כׇּל הַמִּטַּלְטְלִים מְבִיאִין אֶת הַטּוּמְאָה
phrases.english: that all movable objects bring impurity
onto the person who carries them
at the thickness of an ox goad,
and onto themselves at any size.
And onto other people and vessels —
only with an opening of a handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אֲנִי אֲתַקֵּן שֶׁיְּהוּ דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים קַיָּימִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposes רבי טרפון by defending the decree with clear limits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goad-thick movable object makes its carrier טמא. It becomes טמא itself at any size. It affects others only at a טפח.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: the decree is about circumference
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי explains that the ox goad in the decree has a circumference of a טפח but a width of less than a טפח. The חכמים decreed on the circumference because of the width.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: The ox goad the חכמים spoke about has a width of less than a טפח but a circumference of a טפח. They made a decree about its circumference because of its width.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי defines exactly what size ox goad the decree is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An object that is a full טפח wide is a tent by Torah law. A goad whose circumference is a טפח is much thinner, so by Torah law it is not a tent. The חכמים made a rabbinic decree on it anyway, because people might confuse it with a truly טפח-wide object. That is why it counts as a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: Its thickness or width (diameter).
Its circumference, the distance around it.
They decreed. This means a rabbinic enactment.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the goad is a טפח wide. Its distance around is a טפח, so its actual width is only about a third of a טפח.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yannai said:
And the ox goad that they mentioned,
its width is not a handbreadth
but its circumference is a handbreadth —
and they decreed about its circumference because of its width.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the size of the goad in the decree that רבי עקיבא upheld.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The decree covers a goad whose circumference is a טפח. It is a rabbinic extension of the Torah rule for a טפח width.

steps.title: For רבי טרפון, the count of eighteen is short
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if רבי טרפון rejects the ox-goad decree, the list of eighteen decrees is missing one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי טרפון, who said 'I will bury my sons if this ruling is not garbled,' the decrees come up short!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a counting problem. Without the ox-goad decree, רבי טרפון does not have eighteen decrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tradition says eighteen decrees were made on that day. The ox goad was one of them. Since רבי טרפון says it never existed, his list has only seventeen, so the גמרא demands to know where he finds the missing decree.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They are lacking.' The count falls short.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Tarfon, who said
I will bury my sons
if this ruling is not truncated —
they are lacking!
phrases.notes: He means the count comes out short of eighteen decrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן דְּאָמַר אֲקַפֵּחַ אֶת בָּנַי שֶׁהֲלָכָה זוֹ מְקוּפַּחַת בָּצְרוּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי טרפון's view in step 1 and tests it against the count of eighteen.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי טרפון's rejection of the ox-goad decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There must be eighteen decrees. Removing the ox goad leaves only seventeen.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק completes רבי טרפון's count
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the decree on the daughters of כותים was also made that day. He adds that on the other issue (drawn water), רבי טרפון holds like רבי מאיר. This fills out the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The decree that daughters of the כותים are treated as נדות from their cradle was also made on that day. And on the other matter, רבי טרפון holds like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the counting problem. It replaces the ox-goad decree with the כותים decree, and keeps the drawn-water decree in the count, so רבי טרפון still has eighteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי טרפון, the decree about כותים girls is counted among the eighteen. On the separate issue of drawn water (מים שאובין), he follows רבי מאיר, who counts it among the eighteen. So he drops the ox goad but still reaches eighteen.

keyTerms.meaning: Daughters of the כותים (Samaritans).
Treated as נדות (menstruants) from the cradle.
On that very day. This is the day the eighteen decrees were made.
And in the other matter.
He holds (this opinion).

steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון rejects the ox-goad decree and calls it a garbled ruling. רבי עקיבא keeps it with clear limits, and רבי ינאי explains it as a decree on circumference. רבי טרפון still reaches eighteen decrees by counting the כותים decree and following רבי מאיר on the drawn-water issue.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Also, that the daughters of Samaritans are menstruants from their cradle,
they decreed on that day.
And in the other matter, he holds like Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: This is about the drawn-water issue.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אַף בְּנוֹת כּוּתִים נִדּוֹת מֵעֲרִיסָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counting challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Substitution: the כותים decree fills the missing slot in the count.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the ox goad, רבי טרפון has fewer than eighteen decrees.
steps.terutzMaskana: He counts the כותים decree and follows רבי מאיר on drawn water, so he still reaches eighteen.

steps.title: The next decree: harvesting grapes for the press
steps.stepSummary: Another of the eighteen decrees concerns grapes harvested for the wine press. שמאי says the grapes become susceptible to טומאה, and הלל says they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other decree: someone who picks grapes to take to the press. שמאי says the grapes have become able to receive טומאה. הלל says they have not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to listing the eighteen decrees and presents another one of them. It is the case of grapes picked for the wine press.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become טמא after it has been made wet by a liquid that the owner wanted there. This is called הכשר. When grapes are picked for the press, juice leaks out on its own. שמאי says the grapes still become susceptible. The גמרא later explains that this is a protective decree, since the owner does not really want the juice that drips away. הלל says it does not count, since the owner did not intend this juice.

keyTerms.meaning: One who harvests grapes
Wine press
It has become susceptible to טומאה because liquid touched it
The rule that food must first be wetted by a wanted liquid before it can become טמא

steps.confusionAlert: 'הוכשר' does NOT mean the grapes are now טמא. It only means they are now ABLE to become טמא if they touch something impure.

phrases.english: And the other one [of the decrees] —
phrases.notes: Continues the list of eighteen decrees made on that day

phrases.english: one who harvests grapes for the press,
Shammai says: it has become susceptible,
phrases.notes: The גמרא later explains this as a decree

phrases.english: Hillel says: it has not become susceptible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling רבי טרפון's count, the גמרא continues listing the eighteen decrees with another one of them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמאי: grapes picked for the press become susceptible through their seeping juice. הלל: they do not.

steps.title: הלל compares grapes to olives
steps.stepSummary: הלל challenges שמאי: if leaking juice makes grapes susceptible, why do people take care to pick grapes in purity but not olives?
steps.simpleTranslation: הלל said to שמאי: Why do people pick grapes in purity, but they do not pick olives in purity?
steps.whatsHappening: הלל attacks שמאי's position with a comparison. Olives also leak liquid when picked, yet no one is careful about purity when picking olives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grapes and olives both leak liquid when they are harvested. Everyone agrees that olive harvesting is not done in purity. That shows the olives' leaking oil does not make them susceptible. So by the same logic, the grapes' leaking juice should not make the grapes susceptible either.

keyTerms.meaning: In purity, using pure vessels and with care
Harvesting olives

phrases.english: Hillel said to Shammai:
For what reason do they harvest grapes in purity
but they do not harvest olives in purity?
phrases.notes: Olives also leak, so why the difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הִלֵּל לְשַׁמַּאי: מִפְּנֵי מַה
steps.kashyaTarget: שמאי's ruling that seeping grape juice makes grapes susceptible
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inconsistency: olives leak liquid too, yet olive harvesting is not done in purity. Grapes should be treated the same way.

steps.title: שמאי threatens to extend the decree to olives
steps.stepSummary: שמאי answers that if הלל pushes him, he will decree טומאה on olive harvesting too.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמאי said to him: If you provoke me, I will decree טומאה on the olive harvest as well.
steps.whatsHappening: שמאי does not back down. He removes the inconsistency by saying olives should be treated like grapes too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל's challenge worked by pointing to a difference between grapes and olives. שמאי does not explain the difference. Instead, he removes it by extending his strict rule to olives as well. He says the olive practice does not disprove his view, because he is ready to change that practice.

keyTerms.meaning: You provoke or anger me
I will decree
The olive harvest

phrases.english: He said to him: If you provoke me,
I will decree impurity even on the olive harvest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמאי answers הלל's challenge from Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removing the contradiction by extending the strict rule to the comparison case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Olives are harvested without purity, so leaking liquid does not make produce susceptible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The olive practice is no proof. שמאי is ready to apply the same strictness to olives.

steps.title: A sword in the בית המדרש and הלל sitting like a student
steps.stepSummary: The dispute became so intense that a sword was planted at the בית המדרש, and no one was allowed to leave. That day הלל sat humbly before שמאי like a student.
steps.simpleTranslation: They stuck a sword into the בית המדרש and said: Whoever wants to come in may come in, but whoever is inside may not leave. That day הלל sat bent over before שמאי like one of the students.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells the story of the day these decrees were voted on. Everyone was kept inside so the vote would be decided by the people present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blocking the exit kept everyone in the room for the vote. On that day, the students of בית שמאי outnumbered those of בית הלל. הלל was the leader of the generation, yet he sat bowed before שמאי, because שמאי's side held the majority that day.

keyTerms.meaning: They stuck a sword into the ground
The study hall
Bent over, in a humble position

phrases.english: They stuck a sword in the study hall,
they said: whoever enters — may enter,
and whoever wants to leave — may not leave.
phrases.notes: This kept the voters in the room

phrases.english: And that day Hillel was
bowed and sitting before Shammai
like one of the students.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the legal argument to a story about how the decrees were decided.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The decrees were decided by a vote in which שמאי's side held the majority.

steps.title: A day as hard as the day of the Golden Calf
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא judges that day as being as painful for Israel as the day the Golden Calf was made.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that day was as hard for Israel as the day the Golden Calf was made.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the story to give its judgment of that day: it was a very sad day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה normally follows בית הלל. On this day, הלל's side lost the vote and בית שמאי's rulings were set down. Comparing it to the Golden Calf shows how serious a loss this was considered to be.

keyTerms.meaning: Hard, painful
The Golden Calf

phrases.english: And it was as difficult for Israel
as the day on which the Calf was made.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the גמרא's evaluation of the event described in Step 9.

steps.title: The decree was accepted only when the students issued it
steps.stepSummary: When שמאי and הלל issued the decree on grapes, the people did not accept it. When their students issued it later, the people accepted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמאי and הלל made the decree, but the people did not accept it from them. Then their students came and made the decree, and the people accepted it from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends by explaining when this decree actually took effect: in the generation of the students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were two stages. First, שמאי and הלל issued the decree, but it did not take hold. Later, their students issued it again, and the people accepted it. This is why the decree counts among the eighteen decrees of that day.

keyTerms.meaning: They decreed
They accepted it from them
Their students

steps.whatToRemember: The grape-press decree was argued between שמאי and הלל, decided by a vote in which שמאי's side won, and finally accepted only when their students issued it.

phrases.english: And Shammai and Hillel decreed
and they [the people] did not accept it from them,
and their students came and decreed
and they accepted it from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּגְזוּר שַׁמַּאי וְהִלֵּל וְלָא קַבִּלוּ מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story by telling how the decree was finally put into effect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The grape-harvest decree took effect only when the students of שמאי and הלל issued it.

steps.title: Why was this decree made?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the decree that grapes picked for the press are susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now returns to the law itself and asks why the חכמים made this decree. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By basic Torah law, juice that leaks without the owner's intent should not make the grapes susceptible. So the גמרא wants to know what concern led the חכמים to be strict anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the story back to the reasoning behind the decree.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying concern that led the חכמים to decree that grapes picked for the press become susceptible.

steps.title: First reason: impure baskets
steps.stepSummary: רבי זעירי in the name of רבי חנינא says the decree was made in case someone picks the grapes into impure baskets.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זעירי said in the name of רבי חנינא: It is a decree, in case he picks the grapes into impure baskets.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is given to the question of Step 12: the decree protects against a case where the baskets are טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the grapes are in an impure basket, the juice that collects there gets the status of a wanted liquid. That would make the grapes truly susceptible, and they would become טמא from the basket. To prevent mistakes in that case, the חכמים treated all grapes picked for the press as susceptible.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree, made in case something might happen
Impure baskets

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ze'iri said that Rabbi Hanina said:
It is a decree, lest he harvest them
into impure baskets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יִבְצְרֶנּוּ בְּקוּפּוֹת טְמֵאוֹת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree guards against picking grapes into impure baskets, where the juice would count as wanted and make the grapes susceptible.

steps.title: The first reason works only for one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The impure-basket reason works for the opinion that an impure vessel gives liquids the status of wanted liquids. It fails for the opinion that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says an impure vessel makes liquids count as wanted. But according to the one who says an impure vessel does not make liquids count as wanted, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 13. It shows that the answer depends on a disputed rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The impure-basket reason only works if an impure vessel makes the juice count as wanted. One opinion holds that an impure vessel does NOT do this. According to that opinion, the juice in an impure basket still would not make the grapes susceptible, so there is nothing to protect against and the decree would have no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well
An impure vessel makes liquids count as wanted
What can be said?

steps.confusionAlert: 'חושב משקין' does not mean that the vessel 'thinks.' It means the vessel gives the liquid the legal status of a liquid that the owner wanted.

phrases.english: This works out according to the one who says
an impure vessel accords liquids [wanted status] — fine,
but according to the one who says
an impure vessel does not accord liquids [wanted status] —
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כְּלִי טָמֵא חוֹשֵׁב מַשְׁקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The impure-baskets reason of רבי זעירי in the name of רבי חנינא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason depends on the view that an impure vessel gives liquids wanted status. According to the opposing view, impure baskets pose no danger, so the decree has no basis.

steps.title: Second reason: sealed, pitched baskets
steps.stepSummary: רבי זעירי in the name of רבי חנינא gives a new reason: the decree is in case someone picks the grapes into sealed, pitch-lined baskets.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, זעירי said in the name of רבי חנינא: It is a decree, in case he picks the grapes into baskets sealed with pitch.
steps.whatsHappening: The first reason is dropped, and a new reason is given that works according to every opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pitch-lined baskets do not leak, so the juice stays in the basket with the grapes. The owner is happy with this, because it speeds up making wine. That makes the juice truly wanted, so the grapes become susceptible no matter what the basket's purity status is. The חכמים then extended the rule to all grapes picked for the press.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)
Baskets sealed with pitch, so they do not leak

steps.whatToRemember: According to זעירי in the name of רבי חנינא, the decree on grapes for the press rests on the case of sealed, pitched baskets. There, the juice is truly wanted. This reason works even for the opinion that an impure vessel does not give liquids wanted status. רבא gives a different reason in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר זְעֵירִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Ze'iri said that Rabbi Hanina said:
It is a decree, lest he harvest them
into pitched baskets.
phrases.notes: The juice stays inside, and the owner is happy with it

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר זְעֵירִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יִבְצְרֶנּוּ בְּקוּפּוֹת מְזוּפָּפוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14 by replacing the reason given in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the reason with one that works according to every opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree is based on impure baskets, which depends on a disputed rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree is based on sealed baskets that keep the juice in, so the juice is truly wanted according to everyone.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In זעירי's revised explanation, grapes picked for the press were decreed susceptible because of the sealed-basket case, where the juice is genuinely wanted. רבא disputes this in the next step.

steps.title: רבא's reason: grapes stuck together
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the decree on grapes is because of clusters that are stuck together. Separating them squeezes out juice, and that juice makes the grapes able to become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The decree was made because of grape clusters that are stuck together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to the question of step 12, which asked why grapes picked for the press can become impure. His answer is different from רבי זעירי's basket explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become impure after a liquid touches it in a way the owner wants. When a person pulls apart clusters that are stuck together, juice squirts out because of his own action, so it counts as wanted liquid. For this reason רבא does not need to rely on the baskets at all.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who offers his own reason for the decree
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Literally 'biting.' Grape clusters that are stuck or pressed together

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is a decree because of the clusters stuck together.
phrases.notes: Pulling them apart squeezes out juice by the person's own hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new reason for the decree, separate from רבי זעירי's basket-based explanations
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree exists because separating stuck-together clusters squeezes out juice willfully, and that juice makes the grapes susceptible to impurity

steps.title: Juice squeezed to test ripeness stays wet until harvest
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה describes a farmer who squeezes a cluster onto his grapes to test if they are ripe. That juice can still be wet when he harvests them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: Sometimes a person goes to his vineyard to find out whether the grapes are ready to harvest. He takes a cluster, squeezes it, and sprays the juice onto the grapes. At harvest time, that liquid may still be wet on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבא's idea. It shows that juice a person squeezes on purpose in the vineyard can really still be on the grapes at harvest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The farmer squeezes the juice on purpose to test ripeness, so it counts as wanted liquid. The key point is that this moisture can last until the harvest. So the grapes may already be able to become impure when they are picked, and that is why חכמים made a general decree.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who reports this teaching
רב נחמן's teacher, the source of the statement
Harvesting grapes
A cluster of grapes
Sprays or sprinkles liquid
Wet enough to moisten something else it touches

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the decree is based on a real, common situation. Willful moisture can be on the grapes at harvest without anyone noticing.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: As Rav Nachman said that Rabbah bar Avuh said:
Sometimes a person goes to his vineyard

phrases.aramaic: לֵידַע אִם הִגִּיעוּ עֲנָבִים לִבְצִירָה אוֹ לֹא,
phrases.english: to find out whether the grapes have reached harvest time or not,
and he takes a cluster of grapes to squeeze it,
and he sprays the juice onto the grapes,
and at the time of harvest
the liquid is still moist on them.
phrases.notes: Because the juice was squeezed on purpose, it makes the grapes susceptible to impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's reason by showing that willfully squeezed juice can remain on the grapes until harvest
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that juice released by a person's own action is a real concern at harvest
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן quoting רבה בר אבוה about a farmer testing ripeness by squeezing grapes

steps.title: What is the remaining decree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the other decree is, because not all eighteen decrees have been counted yet. The answer starts with 'said' and continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the other one? Said...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is still counting the eighteen decrees, asks what the remaining one is, and begins the answer, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of the grape decree is finished, and the גמרא returns to its larger list of the decrees made on that day. The word 'אמר' introduces someone who will name the missing decree.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning the remaining item still to be identified
The eighteen decrees made on one day by בית שמאי and בית הלל

phrases.english: And the other one? Said
phrases.notes: The name of the speaker and his answer continue on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the grape-decree discussion and returns to listing the eighteen decrees
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the remaining decree among the eighteen
